course_name_original: Spanish B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 1/3
course_name_en: Spanish B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 1/3
prerequisites: Knowledge of Spanish at least at A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: The student can write an understandable informative and argumentative text on general and industry-specific topics, conduct correspondence typical for the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
The student can clearly present their conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.

The student understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they concern industry-specific and current issues, and can interpret the acquired information.

The student can use grammatical structures, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow for understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic and industry-specific texts, and allow for relatively fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
The student can prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry-specific topics and participate in discussions relatively fluently and spontaneously, also in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: Spanish B-2 – compulsory course 135 hours - semester 1/3: Classes within the module are conducted in the form of exercises (135 hours).
GRAMMAR ISSUES: Noun, Deverbal nouns, Nouns derived from adjectives

Personal pronoun: functions, omission, order, form (As subject for clarity, emphasis, expressing opposition; As OD; allowed forms; use when OD precedes the predicate; As OI; use despite the presence of a noun, duplication in evaluative constructions; with a preposition (entre, excepto, salvo, incluso, hasta segun+ pron.pers. sujeto); order and form OI+OD)
Reflexive pronoun: functions (use in impersonal sentences; meaning of reciprocity; modification of the meaning of some verbs (quedarse, irse, tomarse))
Adjective: Formation of adjectives with opposite meaning, Compound adjectives, Order of adjectives and shortened forms
Preposition: Use of 'por' and 'para', Specific use of prepositions in combination with certain verbs and in prepositional phrases
Verb: Functions of impersonal forms (infinitivo, infinitivo compuesto, participio, gerundio)
Morphology and uses of indicative tenses [presente, preterito perfecto, preterito indefinido, preterito imperfecto, preterito pluscuamperfecto, futuro simple i futuro compuesto de indicativo]
Morphology and uses of conditional tenses [condicional simple, condicional compuesto]
Morphology and uses of subjunctive mood [presente, preterito perfecto, preterito imperfecto, preterito pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo]
Passive voice [ser+ participio (+ por + agente)]
Use of periphrastic constructions [e.g.: Estar+participio, Estar+gerundio, acabar+ de+infinit., terminar + de + infinit., volver + a + infinit., llevar + gerundio, ir+ gerundio]
Formation of impersonal constructions
Correlation of tenses in complex subordinate clauses
Use of verbs ser, estar, haber
Important verbs changing meaning depending on the voice (e.g.:poner/ ponerse, quedar/ quedarse) and the accompanying word (e.g.:ponerse + a, ponerse + de)

Words and expressions: indicating logical connections between parts of a sentence (simple, complex); ensuring coherence of speech (oral or written); reflecting the speaker's attitude to the presented content (in a discussion)

Presenting one's own opinion, providing information from other sources, clarifying, organizing speech and adding new arguments, emphasizing a previously given argument, introducing new counterarguments, contrasting elements, ordering information, correcting information, rephrasing, summarizing, explaining/justifying, quoting examples, quoting reasons.
Expressing assumption, hypothesis, condition, concession, cause, effect
Defining temporal relations (succession, antecedence, simultaneity, specific moment or period, initial or final moment, duration)
Reported speech: transformation of individual elements of a sentence/utterance; semantics of verbs denoting an act of communication.
Formation of comparisons and absolute superlative
TOPICS AND VOCABULARY: Professional work: requirements, skills, experiences, expectations and fears, forms of contact with employer and team
Education: My university, faculty and field of study, subjects and forms of classes
Student life (study, norms, duties and limitations, entertainment, additional development opportunities, individual and group work)
Designing products that meet specific requirements (object, place, etc.)
Means and methods of information transfer in the modern world
Political and historical events
Culture: films, performances, readings
Global problems and problems of local communities
Cities: history, attractions, infrastructure, culture, gastronomy
Customs, holidays, local and international traditions
Travel, tourism, tourism industry
State of the natural environment
Pro-health behaviors, physical activity, extreme sports
Interpersonal relationships and lifestyle: family, friends, formal and informal groups, subcultures
Psychological reactions to events and challenges, attitude to incomprehensible phenomena

LANGUAGE FUNCTIONS AND OTHER SKILLS: Giving information, pointing out, specifying, defining, describing; asking for information, giving and supplementing information, asking for confirmation and referring to given information
Asking for opinion/evaluation and expressing opinion/evaluation
Expressing approval/disapproval, support or lack of support
Expressing agreement/disagreement; asking someone for agreement, encouraging agreement
Showing doubt
Presenting arguments and counterarguments
Expressing certainty/obviousness or their absence
Formulating hypotheses
Expressing possibility, probability
Expressing conditions and requirements
Presenting goals and reasons
Expressing necessity or need or their absence
Asking about knowledge of something; expressing knowledge or its absence
Asking about skills and experiences and presenting them to the interlocutor
Asking about preferences and interests and presenting them
Asking about preferences and defining preferences; expressing indifference or lack of preference
Asking about desires/wishes and presenting them
Asking about plans and intentions and presenting them

Asking about emotional experiences and expressing joy, satisfaction, sadness, boredom, satiety, aversion, anger, indignation, fear, anxiety, concern, sympathy, encouragement, hope, disappointment, resignation, remorse, shame, surprise, astonishment, admiration and pride
Defining physical sensations
Giving commands or instructions
Asking for politeness, for an object, for help; offering help in action
Making a request/application and responding
Asking for permission, giving consent/not giving consent; forbidding
Proposing and suggesting solutions, joint actions
Offering, proposing and inviting; accepting an offer or invitation or refusing
Advising, warning, threatening
Reproaching
Making promises and expressing commitment
Calming and comforting
Presenting goals and reasons
Formulating conditions and requirements
Editing texts: private and official emails and letters, e.g., cover letter, CV, applications, requests, complaints, reports
Referring in writing or orally to oral texts (interviews, general conversations, as well as popular science statements)
Reading popular science texts with understanding.
Creating and presenting longer oral statements related to the field of study
assessment_rules: The condition for obtaining credit is a positive grade from all colloquia conducted during the semester. In case of a negative grade from the first attempt, the student is allowed to improve it, resulting in the negative grade being replaced by a positive one that counts towards the average. Improving a grade from the second attempt results in the average of the two grades being entered into the record sheet; the average partial grade for passing the test cannot be less than 3.0. An unjustified absence from a test results in forfeiture of the attempt, and each student has the right to two retake colloquia, which can take place at intervals of not less than 2 days. The final grade for the language course is determined as the arithmetic mean of all grades obtained by the student from the credits of individual semesters and the foreign language exam.
